title: University of Helsinki Scholarship Programme 2027

organization.name: University of Helsinki
organization.about: The University of Helsinki is Finland’s oldest and largest university, located in Helsinki, offering international master’s programmes taught in English.

deadlineText: 19 January 2027. Application period 5–19 January 2027 via Studyinfo.
stipend: 50% or 100% tuition waiver; EUR 5,000/year relocation grant for top candidates
intro: Tuition fee waivers of 50% or 100% for non-EU/EEA fee-paying master’s students at the University of Helsinki. Top candidates may receive a EUR 5,000/year Finland Scholarship. Living costs are not covered.
description:
Overview

The University of Helsinki Scholarship Programme offers tuition fee waivers of 50% or 100% to excellent tuition-fee-liable students from outside the EU/EEA and Switzerland who are admitted to an international master’s programme taught in English. The majority of available waivers are 50%.

Top candidates may also receive a Finland Scholarship: a 100% tuition fee waiver plus a €5,000 annual relocation grant. The university notes that its scholarship programme printed on the official page covers tuition waivers; the Finland Scholarship is a separate national scheme and availability should be confirmed for your programme.

Scholarship Coverage

Tuition fees and scholarship options at the University of Helsinki
ItemDetails
Tuition fees (without a waiver)€13,000, €15,000 or €18,000 per academic year depending on the programme; the individual student’s fee stays the same throughout the programme.
50% tuition fee waiverCovers half of the tuition fee. This is the most common award.
100% tuition fee waiverCovers the full tuition fee. Awarded to the best candidates; limited numbers.
Finland Scholarship (where offered)100% tuition fee waiver plus a €5,000 relocation grant, renewed for year two if you complete at least 55 ECTS in year one.
Duration and renewalScholarships cover two years. Continuation into year two requires at least 55 ECTS earned in the first study year.
Not coveredLiving expenses, and (for scholarships starting in 2026 or later) the HYY student union fee.

Eligibility

  • You are eligible for an international master’s programme at the University of Helsinki and are liable for tuition fees: citizens of non-EU/EEA countries without permanent residence status in Finland ( Switzerland also treated as outside the fee-liable group for waiver purposes).
  • You meet the requirements for a Finnish entry visa and residence permit.
  • You have excellent results in previous studies and can prove this in your application.
  • English requirement for international master’s programmes: IELTS 6.5 with a minimum of 6.0 per section, TOEFL iBT 92, PTE 68, or Cambridge C1–C2 (check your programme for specifics).

Application Timeline and Process

Key dates for the autumn 2027 intake
ItemDetails
Application period5–19 January 2027 via the Studyinfo.fi national portal.
Deadline19 January 2027.
National application fee€100 for non-EU/EEA applicants, paid in Studyinfo — a one-time fee covering all applications for the same term, and it cannot be waived.
Scholarship applicationApply for the waiver on the same master’s application form — there is no separate scholarship form.
ResultThe waiver decision arrives with your admission result in the official acceptance email; you must then sign a scholarship agreement.

How to Apply

  • Find your master’s programme in the University of Helsinki programme search and prepare the required attachments, including English-test results.
  • Apply to the master’s programme through Studyinfo.fi between 5 and 19 January 2027 and pay the €100 national application fee if applicable.
  • Apply for the 50% or 100% tuition fee waiver within the same application form and submit all required attachments.
  • If offered a scholarship, accept the place and sign the scholarship agreement by the stated deadline, or the award is cancelled.

Official Link

University of Helsinki — tuition fees and scholarship programme

Important Notes

  • Helsinki living costs are high — plan a strong personal budget even with a tuition waiver.
  • The application fee is non-refundable and does not guarantee admission.
  • Reserve lists are not used and a declined scholarship cannot be transferred to another student.
